body.statement:
Let \(P\) be a fixed interior law covered by Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), where the deterministic complete-normal incidence basis uses every period-admissible OVS clean cohort \(\mathcal C_u=\{c\in\mathcal G:c>u\}\) for every restricted post-period \(u\).  Suppose \(X\) has fixed finite support \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\), every support mass is positive, retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition hold, and \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are i.i.d.  Fix \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\), and impose the stated local-rank and positive-spectrum conditions on its finite KKT system.

Let \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{ret}}\) be the finite set of cohort--eligibility cells appearing in a target score or in a complete OVS normal.  Define the observable finite vector \(U(O)\) by the coordinates
\[
U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}=\mathbf 1\{X=x_d,G=a,S=s\},
\quad
U^{(1)}_{d,a,s,u}=U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}\Delta Y_u,
\quad
U^{(2)}_{d,a,s,u,v}=U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v,
\]
for \(d=1,\ldots,D\), \((a,s)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{ret}}\), and \(u,v\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), and put \(\mu=E_P[U(O)]\).  From a generic moment vector \(z\), reconstruct
\[
P_z(X=x_d)=\sum_{a,s}z^{(0)}_{d,a,s},
\qquad
p_{a,s,z}(x_d)=\frac{z^{(0)}_{d,a,s}}{P_z(X=x_d)},
\]
\[
m_{a,s,u,z}(x_d)=\frac{z^{(1)}_{d,a,s,u}}{z^{(0)}_{d,a,s}},
\qquad
E_z[\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v\mid X=x_d,G=a,S=s]
=\frac{z^{(2)}_{d,a,s,u,v}}{z^{(0)}_{d,a,s}}.
\tag{16}
\]
Use (16) and Definitions \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\) to form \(\theta_z\), \(\Psi_z\), \(\Omega_z=E_z[\Psi_z\Psi_z^{\prime}]\), \(\psi_z^0\), \(K_z(x_d)\), and \(r_z(x_d)\); every expectation here is evaluated from the displayed first and second cross-moments.  Solve the relevant blockwise or joint comparator KKT system at \(\Omega_z\) for \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}_z\), and define the explicit finite-dimensional map
\[
F_{\mathrm{cmp}}(z)
=b_z^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Omega_zb_z^{\mathrm{cmp}}
-\left\{E_z[(\psi_z^0)^2]
-\sum_{d=1}^DP_z(X=x_d)r_z(x_d)^{\prime}K_z(x_d)^{\dagger}r_z(x_d)\right\}.
\tag{17}
\]
Then \(F_{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mu)=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\).

Set \(\widehat\mu=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nU(O_i)\), take \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\) with \(0<a<1/4\), replace every scalar probability denominator in (16) and in the subsequent score and normal reconstruction, including every target share \(\pi_{g,1}\), by its maximum with \(\tau_n\), and replace every Moore--Penrose inverse of a complete-normal matrix or comparator KKT matrix by the inverse retaining exactly the eigenvalues whose absolute values exceed \(\tau_n\).  Denote the resulting everywhere-defined map by \(F_{\mathrm{cmp},\tau_n}\) and set
\[
\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}
=F_{\mathrm{cmp},\tau_n}(\widehat\mu).
\tag{18}
\]
Let \(F^{\circ}_{\widehat{\mathfrak r}}\) be the differentiable branch of (17) that retains the ranks selected in (18), calculate
\[
\widehat d= D F^{\circ}_{\widehat{\mathfrak r}}(\widehat\mu),
\qquad
\widehat\zeta_i=\widehat d^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\},
\qquad
\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\zeta_i^2,
\tag{19}
\]
where every inverse derivative is evaluated by the formula in Lemma \(\ref{lem:separated-spectral-delta}\).  Thus (18)--(19) are computable from empirical cell counts, first moments, and second cross-moments only.

Write \(d_P=DF^{\circ}_{\mathfrak r_P}(\mu)\) and \(\zeta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp},P}(O)=d_P^{\prime}\{U(O)-\mu\}\).  If
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\geq\delta_0>0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
0<V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
:=E_P[(\zeta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp},P})^2]<\infty,
\tag{20}
\]
then
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\zeta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp},P}(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}),
\tag{21}
\]
\[
\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
\longrightarrow_P V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}},
\qquad
\frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\}}
{\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}}}
\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{22}
\]
The corresponding two-sided Wald interval has pointwise limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\), and its lower endpoint is positive with probability tending to one.  This conclusion is pointwise at the fixed support and fixed ranks; it makes no continuous-covariate, growing-support, or rank-uniform claim.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove that (17) is the desired observed-law functional.  Because \(T\), the retained cell set, and the support of \(X\) are finite, each coordinate of a pairwise score or complete normal is, conditional on \((X,G,S)\), an affine function of \((\Delta Y_2,\ldots,\Delta Y_T)\).  Its conditional mean therefore depends only on the coordinates \(U^{(0)}\) and \(U^{(1)}\), and every conditional product of two such coordinates depends only on \(U^{(0)}\), \(U^{(1)}\), and \(U^{(2)}\).  The first two lines of (16) hence reconstruct \(p\), \(m\), \(q\), \(\pi\), and \(\theta\); the last line reconstructs every shared-cell cross-period covariance.  It follows directly from Definitions \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and \(\ref{def:complete-normal-projection}\) that \(\Omega\), \(E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]\), \(K_P(x_d)\), and \(r_P(x_d)\) are exactly their values reconstructed from \(\mu\).  In particular, no independence between score coordinates sharing an outcome cell has been imposed.

Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), applied to the deterministic basis of all period-admissible OVS rows in the premise, gives
\[
V_{\mathrm{can}}
=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
-\sum_{d=1}^DP(X=x_d)r_P(x_d)^{\prime}K_P(x_d)^{\dagger}r_P(x_d).
\tag{23}
\]
The observable equalities give \(E_P[\Psi_P]=0\).  Hence the variance of the fixed comparator score is
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}
=b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{cmp}}.
\tag{24}
\]
The comparator definitions identify \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\) with the loading coordinate of the corresponding Moore--Penrose KKT solution.  Subtracting (23) from (24) proves
\[
F_{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mu)
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{can}}
=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P).
\tag{25}
\]
Thus the causal efficiency target, the observed-law gap functional, and its estimator remain distinct: (25) identifies the second, while (18) estimates it.

Retained-cell overlap and the positive support masses imply
\[
\min_{d,(a,s)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{ret}}}
E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]>0.
\tag{26}
\]
The fourth-moment assumption gives
\(
|\Delta Y_u|^4\leq8(|Y_u|^4+|Y_{u-1}|^4)
\leq16\max_{t\in\mathcal T}|Y_t|^4
\), so Cauchy--Schwarz gives, for all \(u,v\),
\[
E_P[(U^{(2)}_{d,a,s,u,v})^2]
\leq E_P[|\Delta Y_u|^2|\Delta Y_v|^2]
\leq\{E_P[|\Delta Y_u|^4]E_P[|\Delta Y_v|^4]\}^{1/2}<\infty.
\tag{27}
\]
All coordinates of \(U\) consequently have finite variance.  Since its dimension is fixed, Chebyshev's inequality coordinate by coordinate yields
\[
\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{28}
\]

On the neighborhood supplied by (26), the scalar ratios in (16), and hence every reconstructed first or second moment, are continuously differentiable functions of \(z\).  The relevant matrices are finite continuously differentiable matrix functions of \(z\).  At the fixed law, take the minimum over the nonzero absolute eigenvalues of all finitely many \(K_P(x_d)\) and comparator KKT matrices; the minimum is strictly positive, with the zero-rank matrices omitted.  The stipulated comparator spectrum supplies the same conclusion for its KKT matrices.  Since \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n=n^{-1/2+a}\to0\), Lemma \(\ref{lem:separated-spectral-delta}\), (26), and (28) show that, with probability tending to one, scalar clipping is inactive and every matrix rank is recovered.  On that event
\[
F_{\mathrm{cmp},\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)
=F^{\circ}_{\mathfrak r_P}(\widehat\mu),
\qquad
\widehat d=DF^{\circ}_{\mathfrak r_P}(\widehat\mu).
\tag{29}
\]
The local-rank premise identifies this selected branch with the ordinary comparator functional along regular model submodels.  Formula (14) makes all generalized-inverse derivatives explicit, so the derivative in (19) is computable rather than existential.

Continuous differentiability and (28)--(29) now give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)
&=d_P^{\prime}(\widehat\mu-\mu)+o_P(n^{-1/2})\\
&=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
d_P^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\mu\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
The summands in the last line are i.i.d. and mean zero.  Their variance is finite by (27) and is positive by (20).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\), applied to these scalar summands, proves (21).

It remains to verify studentization.  Equation (29) and continuity of the derivative imply \(\widehat d\to_Pd_P\).  Moreover, the weak law following from (27) gives
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|U(O_i)-\mu\|^2=O_P(1),
\qquad \|\widehat\mu-\mu\|=o_P(1).
\tag{31}
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz, (31), and \(\widehat d-d_P=o_P(1)\),
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[
\widehat d^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}
-d_P^{\prime}\{U(O_i)-\mu\}
\right]^2=o_P(1).
\tag{32}
\]
The weak law for the squared fixed influence value, followed by (32), proves the variance consistency in (22).  To obtain the studentized limit without an additional theorem, fix \(\epsilon>0\).  On the event
\(
|\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/
V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}-1|\leq\epsilon
\), whose probability tends to one, the studentized statistic is bounded between deterministic \((1\pm\epsilon)^{-1/2}\) rescalings of the statistic in (21).  Letting \(n\to\infty\) and then \(\epsilon\downarrow0\), continuity of the standard normal distribution function proves the second assertion of (22) and the stated two-sided Wald coverage.

Finally, (20), (21), and variance consistency imply
\[
\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mathrm{cmp}}
-z_{1-\alpha/2}
\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n}
=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)+o_P(1)
\geq\delta_0+o_P(1).
\tag{33}
\]
Therefore the lower endpoint is positive with probability tending to one.  The argument used neither nuisance-rate assumptions nor a growing dictionary; its finite-support and fixed-law spectral separation are exactly the announced scope.
